name: Envoy
summary: A high-concurrency proxy that separates main-thread coordination from worker-local event loops, composes protocol behavior through filter chains, and distributes dynamic configuration to worker state.

features.name: Main and worker dispatcher topology
features.description: Envoy uses one main thread for coordination and a configurable set of worker threads for listening, filtering, and forwarding traffic. Each main or worker thread runs an Event::Dispatcher, and an accepted connection remains bound to one worker for its lifetime.
benefits: Keeps high-volume connection work on parallel worker event loops
Gives configuration and administration a distinct coordination thread
Reduces locking on the common connection path through worker affinity
costs: Cross-thread posting and worker-local state require explicit synchronization rules
Long-lived connections can create uneven work distribution
Blocking extensions must be isolated from non-blocking dispatchers

features.name: Protocol-independent filter chains
features.description: Envoy composes network and HTTP processing as ordered filter chains. HTTP decoder and encoder filters can operate without knowing the underlying HTTP protocol, pause and resume iteration, and share state within a request stream.
benefits: Adds policy and transformation stages without coupling each filter to wire protocols
Makes ordering and terminal behavior explicit in configuration
Allows filters to participate in routing, authorization, buffering, and observability
costs: Filter ordering becomes part of request semantics and security review
Pausing iteration introduces backpressure and lifecycle states
Route mutation can invalidate decisions made by earlier filters

features.name: Worker-local upstream state with batched updates
features.description: The cluster manager maintains upstream cluster state on the main thread and posts updates to worker dispatchers. Worker-local load balancers can rebuild from a batched priority-set update, while connection pools and async clients use the worker dispatcher.
benefits: Keeps request-path upstream decisions close to the worker that serves them
Publishes coherent configuration batches instead of partial mutations
Separates control-plane discovery from data-plane connection work
costs: Updates must cross thread boundaries before every worker observes new state
Worker-local copies consume memory and can briefly differ during propagation
Cluster and connection-pool lifecycles add coordination complexity

mathematical_views.question: How do main-thread coordination, worker dispatchers, timers, and thread-affine connections advance proxy work?
assumptions: Each dispatcher is modeled as a non-blocking event-loop vertex
An accepted connection remains associated with one worker unless an explicit balancing mechanism intervenes
Posted callbacks are modeled as cross-thread edges rather than shared arbitrary mutation

mathematical_views.question: Which filter callbacks and route decisions are applied to a request or response stream, and in what order?
assumptions: Filters are ordered nodes with decoder and encoder directions
A filter may stop iteration and later continue it
The model abstracts protocol framing while retaining route and filter-state mutations

mathematical_views.question: When does a dynamic upstream update become a coherent worker-local routing and connection state?
assumptions: Main-thread discovery produces an update batch
Worker dispatchers apply the batch through posted callbacks
The view does not infer convergence latency or availability guarantees

benefits: Parallel non-blocking connection processing with a clear coordination boundary
costs: Thread affinity and cross-thread work publication complicate extension design

benefits: Composable protocol policy and transformation stages
costs: Filter order, pausing, and route mutation expand the request state space

benefits: Fast worker-local load balancing and connection-pool access
costs: Batched propagation and duplicated state require update coordination
